ranking.note: Raised to P1: removing LevelDB's exclusive lock is the category-defining unlock for external consumers (concurrent indexers) that the kernel exists to serve.

Raised to P1: deadlock risk when consumer callbacks log, plus a misleading multi-connection API, is a boundary thread-safety/correctness problem and forces a design decision the rest of the logging work depends on.
Placed ahead of #30342 because #30342 explicitly depends on it.

inconsistencies: Logging API: #34775 (one global logging connection per process, levels on the connection handle) and #33847/#30342 (connections attached per context, per-connection levels, per-context routing) pull the public C API in opposite directions. These cannot both land as written; review #34775 first since it is the narrower deadlock/semantics fix, and settle the single-vs-per-context model before #33847 and #30342.

Logging chain order: #33847 must precede #30342 (stated dependency), and #30342 additionally depends on #34778, #34374, #29256 which are not in this category list; #36584 (opaque btck_LogEntry) touches the same header and should be sequenced after the connection model is decided to avoid rework.

Error-reporting overlap: #29700 (util::Result/FlushResult returns for fatal errors), #35646 (remove M_ERROR from ValidationState via util::Expected) and #36326 (typed FatalError/FlushError notifications instead of bilingual_str) all restructure fatal/runtime error propagation across the kernel boundary and partly rewrite the same call sites and C API callbacks. Decide the target shape on #29700 first; #35646 additionally unblocks #35570.
#36318 and #35646 both change ValidationState invariants/semantics and the kernel C API's reporting of invalid results; they will conflict and should be coordinated.

#32427 is both kernel and storage/validation: replacing the block tree database changes on-disk format and block storage logic well beyond the kernel API, and likely needs splitting (format/WAL layer vs kernel-facing consumer access).

#35662 bundles a genuine kernel C API fix (unintended copy of caller txdata) with a validation-side micro-optimization of PrecomputedTransactionData; the API fix is the only part with kernel-category value and would be reviewable faster if split.
result.notes: The list is heavily clustered in P2 because most of these PRs are genuine API-completeness or node-decoupling work, which is exactly the category's core. The two P1s are the ones with reliability/consumer-blocking consequences. Documentation-only PRs (#36353, #36632) and surface-trimming (#33820, #36584) sit in P3 per the category rule that cosmetic API polish without a requesting consumer is P3 or below; #36353 is notable in that it documents a real validation-skipping hazard that arguably deserves a code fix rather than a warning.
